general.summary: Input scope, assumptions, counterexamples and goal preservation.
hints: Start from the original requirement and public contract: identify allowed inputs, states, outputs and observable behavior. Keep unresolved interpretations explicit.

Trace every added precondition to evidence. Special-case tests do not replace the unrestricted case; assumptions, filtering or preprocessing must not remove an allowed boundary or branch before validation.
Look for a counterexample that separates the proposed implementation from the required behavior. Cover meaningful endpoints and both sides of a transition where the domain permits them.
Obtain expected behavior from requirements or independent public evidence, not from the implementation being tested. Undefined behavior, a required error and a valid result are different outcomes.

Turn applicable reminders into checks of the actual entry and deliverable. Record unverified gaps; passing selected checks does not prove complete coverage, and apparent simplicity is not a reason to skip review.

math.summary: Domains, singularities, limits and probability endpoints.
hints: Check the stated number domain and function domain before division, roots, logarithms, inverse functions or powers. Zero denominators and invalid-domain inputs require specified behavior, not an invented restriction.

At singularities, discontinuities and piecewise transitions, distinguish the value at the point, one-sided limits, two-sided limits and any explicitly defined extension. Do not substitute one for another.
Verify that cancellation, simplification or added symbolic assumptions preserve the allowed domain and branches. Test the general expression as well as any justified special cases.
Check signs, periodic boundaries, branch choices, indeterminate forms and empty or degenerate aggregates when relevant. Confirm endpoint inclusion from the contract.
For probabilities, check 0 and 1, normalization, impossible or certain events and empty support. Conditioning on zero probability or assuming independence needs explicit justification.

numeric.summary: Precision, overflow, rounding, money and units.
hints: Check representable minima and maxima, overflow, underflow and loss of precision. Decide from the contract whether non-finite values and signed zero are supported or rejected.
Check cancellation, accumulated error and comparisons near a tolerance threshold. Choose tolerances from an accuracy requirement or justified error bound, not to make a result pass.
Verify rounding direction, halfway cases and the stage where rounding occurs. Money, percentages and integer conversions can change at these boundaries.
Track units and scale through every conversion, including inverse conversions and mixed-unit inputs. A numerically plausible result can still have the wrong unit.
Include negative values, zero, very small and very large magnitudes where allowed. Clamping or coercion must not silently replace the required result or error.

collections.summary: Empty collections, singleton cases, indexing and ordering.
hints: Check empty, singleton and multiple-element inputs. Distinguish a missing collection from a present empty collection when the interface does.
Check first and last positions, inclusive versus exclusive endpoints, lengths and out-of-range access. Negative indices must follow the documented convention.
Check duplicates, missing keys, equality rules and stable ordering. Set-like behavior must not accidentally replace sequence or multiset behavior.
For slicing, pagination and iteration, check exact page boundaries, partial final pages, termination and no missing or duplicated elements.
Check mutation during iteration, shared elements and aliasing where supported. Large collections and deeply nested data should respect documented resource limits.

text.summary: Unicode, whitespace, escaping, parsing and text limits.
hints: Distinguish missing text, empty text, whitespace-only text and valid content. Trimming or normalization must be authorized by the interface.
Check Unicode, combining characters and the unit used for length or positions: bytes, code points or user-perceived characters are not interchangeable.
Check encoding failures, line endings, case rules and locale-sensitive operations. Invalid input must not be silently reported as an empty successful result.
Check delimiters, escaping and nested syntax across parse or serialization boundaries. Treat data as data rather than executable code, paths or instructions.
Check long lines, size limits and truncation. Preserve exact text where required, and distinguish partial content from a complete read or parse.
Identify legal states and transitions, including uninitialized, active, completed, cancelled and failed states. Do not assume a previous step succeeded without evidence.
Check partial initialization and failure after each meaningful side effect. Cleanup must release owned resources without deleting another operation's state.
Check repeated use, restart and interrupted recovery. Preserve committed work and counters; an unknown outcome is not proof that nothing happened.
Check aliasing, stale caches, resource ownership and lifetime. Restoring a value is not enough if associated handles or dependent state remain invalid.
Verify cancellation and termination conditions, including blocked work. Report incomplete cleanup or recovery instead of converting it into success.

time.summary: Time zones, calendar boundaries and clock behavior.
hints: Distinguish instants, local dates, durations and calendar periods. State the time zone and endpoint convention used by comparisons or windows.
Check ambiguous and nonexistent local times, offset changes and conversion across zones. Do not assume every local day has the same duration.
Check midnight, month and year transitions, leap-day handling and expired or exactly-on-deadline inputs as applicable.
Use a clock appropriate to the contract: wall-clock adjustments can break elapsed-time assumptions. Check timestamp precision and conversion rounding.
Check ordering of delayed or out-of-order events, repeated timestamps and interval overlap. Define the treatment of missing or invalid dates from evidence.

permissions.summary: Identity, authorization, thresholds and scope changes.
hints: Separate authenticated identity from authorization for the requested resource and operation. Check both allowed and denied cases, including missing credentials.
Check ownership, tenant or project boundaries and inherited permissions. Access to metadata or a parent object does not automatically authorize child content or writes.
Check expiration, revocation and permission changes between checking and acting. Bind approval to the actual action and resource when required.
For eligibility rules, check the threshold and adjacent values using the stated units, dates and inclusivity. Do not invent legal or business policy from a generic reminder.
Check denied-path behavior for unintended side effects or information disclosure. Defaults and error handling must not silently grant broader access.

concurrency.summary: Races, atomicity, ordering, transactions and idempotence.
hints: Identify shared state and required invariants. Test meaningful overlapping operations and alternate orderings rather than only a sequential successful run.
Check the gap between validation and use, lost updates, duplicate work and stale reads. A lock is useful only if all relevant accesses obey its scope.
Check transaction commit, rollback and partial failure across resources. A local success may not prove that the whole operation committed.
Check retry and duplicate delivery against the promised idempotence and ordering. An uncertain response must not silently trigger a second side effect.
Check deadlock, starvation, cancellation and shutdown while work is active. Completion must mean that owned work and required callbacks have actually finished.

external_io.summary: Network and file failures, partial results and retries.
hints: Check unavailable dependencies, timeout, disconnection and malformed responses. Distinguish a complete empty result from an incomplete or failed operation.
Check partial reads and writes, interrupted transfers and size limits. Validate completeness and integrity before using or publishing a result.
Decide retry behavior from operation semantics and confirmed outcomes. Preserve unknown results and avoid replaying non-idempotent operations blindly.
Check file existence, path scope, access failures and changes during reading or writing. Report disk exhaustion and persistence failure without claiming the operation was saved.
Check dependency version or protocol mismatches and bounded resource use. Fallbacks must preserve the original contract rather than silently weaken it.

generation.summary: Generated artifacts, conversion semantics and real consumption.
hints: Invoke the requested producer with inputs allowed by the original contract. A related API, substitute artifact or specially restricted input does not establish general correctness.
Pass the unchanged actual artifact to its intended consumer. Check successful parsing, compilation or loading where applicable before relying on execution results.
Check semantic preservation across conversions, including conditions, escaping, types, units and exceptional values. Similar-looking output can behave differently.
Exercise general and boundary inputs through the complete producer-to-consumer path. Pre-simplification or hand-written wrappers must not remove the behavior under test.
Use independent expected behavior and retain evidence linking the producer input, artifact and consumer result. Text matching or a round trip alone may hide a shared error.

interaction.summary: Empty, loading, error, cancellation and repeated-action flows.
hints: Check empty, loading, ready and error states and the transitions between them. Visible success must correspond to a confirmed underlying result.
Check repeated clicks or submissions, cancellation, navigation away and return while work is active. Prevent unintended duplicate actions and stale result replacement.
Check invalid and partially entered input, focus or selection changes and available recovery paths. Validation messages must match what the system actually accepts.
Check permission changes, offline behavior and delayed updates. Disabled controls alone do not enforce authorization or prevent concurrent state changes.
For user-facing behavior, check applicable keyboard, assistive-technology, locale and layout constraints from the requirements. Do not silently turn optional reminders into new product requirements.
